canon.name: the priests (group)
canon.note: The priestly class of the sons of Aaron who perform the rites of offering in Leviticus and who repair gates, take part in processions and sign the covenant in Nehemiah; both entries are the same priestly body, so they are one cluster.

stages.label: the priests (group)

quotes.quote: Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood
and some of the priests’ sons with trumpets

stages.text: The priests: adult men, mostly between thirty and fifty, sturdy and unhurried in bearing. Olive to deep bronze skin, short dark or greying beard, close-cropped hair under a linen head covering. Calm, dignified faces. Signature outfit: a white linen tunic and sash, with a plain linen mitre, in cream and off-white. Props: a bronze censer or a trumpet for processional scenes.

aliases: Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah and the Levites
canon.name: The Levites who teach the law (Nehemiah)
canon.note: Levites in Nehemiah who explain the law, lead prayer and confession, and appear in the register of priests and Levites; they are a teaching and prayer group rather than the tabernacle service crew.

stages.label: The Levites who teach the law

quotes.quote: Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law

stages.text: The Levites who teach the law: men of middle age, lean and sure-footed, with brown skin weathered by the Judean sun. Dark hair worn to the shoulder, beards trimmed short and neat. canon.name: Judah (kingdom and land)
canon.note: The kingdom or land of Judah as a single place across Nehemiah, Isaiah, Joel, Habakkuk and Zephaniah; all entries describe the same territory, distinguished only by the section context in which they appear.

stages.label: Judah

its gates have been consumed with fire
some of the children of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns

stages.text: Judah: a hill country of terraced slopes, stony ridges and deep valleys, with walled towns and villages set among olive groves, vineyards and grain fields; Jerusalem on its heights with stone walls, gates and a temple, and fortified citadels; cypress, terebinth and cedar on the uplands.

canon.name: Asaph
canon.note: Levitical singer to whom psalms 50 and 73 to 83 are attributed; the psalmist, distinct from the family of Korah.

stages.label: Asaph, Levitical psalmist

quotes.quote: A Psalm by Asaph.

stages.text: Asaph: a man of middle years, broad-shouldered and steady; olive skin, dark close-cropped beard with grey beginning at the chin, deep-set thoughtful eyes and a worn, weathered face. Plain undyed linen tunic with a dark blue-grey wool cloak, Levitical singer's linen. Carries a ten-stringed lyre of cedar wood.

canon.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

canon.name: Moses
canon.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: Pharaoh (king of Egypt who did not know Joseph)
canon.name: Pharaoh of the Exodus (oppressor of Israel)
canon.note: The unnamed king of Egypt in Exodus who enslaves Israel, hardens his heart against Moses and suffers the plagues; the same king recalled in Deuteronomy and cited in Romans 9:17 as the one raised up to show God's power.

stages.label: Pharaoh of the Exodus

quotes.quote: The king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them
Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them

stages.text: Pharaoh of the Exodus: man in his fifties, tall and broad-shouldered, dark brown skin; close-cropped hair under a blue-and-gold nemes headcloth, and a short trimmed false beard of the royal style; calm, hard features with heavy-lidded eyes and a firm mouth. canon.name: the Egyptians
canon.note: The Egyptian people, officers and magicians in Exodus who oppress Israel and suffer the plagues; distinguished from the Egyptian magicians of Genesis and from the Chaldeans of Babylon.

stages.label: the Egyptians

quotes.quote: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,
They also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same thing with their enchantments.

stages.text: the Egyptians: adults of middle age, broad-shouldered and strong from labour and rank, with warm brown skin and close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven men with short wigs or bare heads, dignified and grave of face. Signature outfit: a pleated white linen kilt or wrap-tunic with a linen cloak in ochre and blue. Signature props: none carried alone; officers may bear a staff of office.

canon.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

canon.name: Red Sea
canon.note: The sea in Exodus that parts for Israel and closes over Pharaoh's army; distinct from the other seas by its setting in the exodus narrative.

stages.label: Red Sea

quotes.quote: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night
the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.

stages.text: Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.

canon.name: The wilderness (Exodus route)
canon.note: The desert stretches Israel travels from Egypt through Shur, Sin and Marah, with manna, quail and water miracles; the same wilderness as the Psalms and Amos references.

stages.label: The wilderness (Exodus route)

quotes.quote: they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.

stages.text: The wilderness: a vast arid tableland of pale sand, gravel plains and dark rock outcrops rising to bare mountains, scattered with thorn scrub and sparse grasses in the wadis. Tents and camp-circles mark the encampments; a distant mountain, Sinai, rises above the plain. Dry riverbeds, stone wells and rock fissures suggest hidden water.

quotes.quote: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite

canon.name: Job
canon.note: Blameless, wealthy man of Uz who loses his family and health and debates with his friends and with Yahweh.

houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust

canon.name: Moses
canon.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

canon.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
canon.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. aliases: those who came out of Egypt

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
canon.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
canon.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. fields.composition: Eye-level view from within the court, the south gate centred, the measuring figure and Ezekiel placed in the foreground at either side of the posts.

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.

canon.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

fields.primarySubject: Isaiah in a plain prophet's mantle, standing upright and facing a cluster of robed rulers.
fields.action: Isaiah raises an open hand while addressing the rulers; a brilliant white-gold radiance, veiled by slow cloud with a fire-like glow at its heart, hangs above the street.
fields.setting: A dusty stone-walled street of Jerusalem near the gate and palace precincts, with the citadel rising behind.
fields.secondaryElements: Court officials in tunics and court robes gathered before him, listening with guarded expressions; a stone gate arch and walls in dim light.
fields.mood: Tense, solemn and confrontational, with weighty authority.
fields.timeOfDay: Night turning toward dawn; heavy low cloud, dry still air and a faint haze of dust, with dim radiance falling across the walls.
fields.composition: Medium shot from a low angle at street level, Isaiah at left in profile toward the rulers at right, the radiance and cloud filling the upper frame.

stages.label: John the seer

quotes.quote: to his servant, John
I John, your brother and partner with you in the oppression

stages.text: John the seer: man of about sixty, of middle height and spare build, weathered olive skin from exile by the sea, short greying hair and a close grey beard, lined brow and steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a rough dark brown wool mantle. He carries a worn wooden staff and a small scroll case.

canon.name: New Jerusalem
canon.note: Holy city descending from heaven with twelve gates (Revelation).

stages.label: New Jerusalem

quotes.quote: I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God
showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God
the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from my God
out of the holy city, which are written in this book

stages.text: New Jerusalem: a great and high city descending out of heaven, luminous and pure as crystal, its walls of jasper set on twelve foundations adorned with precious stones, and twelve gates of pearl. Its streets are pure gold, clear as glass, with no temple and no sun or moon, lit by the glory of God. Beside it flows a river of life, clear as crystal, and on its banks stands the tree of life bearing fruit each month.

fields.primarySubject: God's presence shown as brilliant white-gold radiance with a fire-like glow, veiled by slow cloud above an empty throne; John standing and turned toward it.
fields.action: The voice speaks the promise of renewal from the radiance while John listens, ready to write.
fields.setting: A throne-room of heaven under a clear sky, with a glass-like sea spreading before the jeweled city's gates.
fields.secondaryElements: John in an undyed ochre-brown linen tunic under a dark brown wool mantle; a writing tablet and stylus in his hands; the city's walls and gates in jewel tones; an altar at the edge.
fields.mood: Reverent, hopeful and awed, with quiet solemnity.
fields.timeOfDay: Unchanging heavenly daylight, still clear air with faint fire-glow at the throne's edge.
fields.composition: Wide view from slightly below the throne, with the radiance centered high, John in the lower left and the city gates receding to the right.

canon.name: Adam
canon.note: The first man formed from dust in Eden, husband of Eve and father of Cain, Abel and Seth; the Genesis narrative figure, joined by the 1 Corinthians and 1 Timothy references to the same first man.

stages.label: Adam

quotes.quote: there he put the man whom he had formed
to cultivate and keep it
Yahweh God made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.
All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred thirty years, then he died.

stages.text: Adam: a full-grown man in early middle age, sturdy and weathered from labour in the ground; broad shoulders, lean strong arms, dark brown skin darkened by sun; short dark curly hair and a close-cut beard; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen wrap over one shoulder, later a simple garment of tawny animal skin; sandals of leather. No signature props, though he is often shown with a hoe or digging tool.

canon.name: Eve
canon.note: The first woman in Genesis, made from Adam's rib and deceived by the serpent; the other two entries (2 Corinthians 11:3 and 1 Timothy 2:14) refer back to this same Eve.

stages.label: Eve

quotes.quote: she would be the mother of all the living

stages.text: Eve: a woman in early adulthood, slender and strong, with a grounded, unhurried bearing. Warm olive-brown skin, dark eyes, long black hair bound back with a linen band. Her face is open and calm, with a serious, dignified expression. Signature outfit: a simple undyed linen wrap over one shoulder, falling to the knee, in ochre and sand tones. Carries no props alone.

canon.name: the serpent of Eden
canon.note: The subtle serpent of the garden who deceives Eve and is cursed in Genesis; the Corinthians reference points back to this same serpent.

stages.label: The serpent of Eden

quotes.quote: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made.
you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the field. You shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.

stages.text: The serpent of Eden: an adult serpent of the field, long and sinuous, its body sleek and scaled in dull olive and dark ochre banded with pale bone-yellow, with a broad flattened head and cold, watchful eyes. Before the curse it is upright-bodied, slender and graceful, showing it was more subtle than the animals of the field; afterward it lies low, dusty, and close to the ground.

canon.name: Garden of Eden
canon.note: The garden planted by Yahweh God in Genesis, with the tree of life and forbidden tree; distinct from the garden in Song of Solomon and the garden across the Kidron.

stages.label: Garden of Eden

quotes.quote: Yahweh God planted a garden eastward, in Eden
including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.
he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way

stages.text: Garden of Eden: a well-watered garden planted eastward in Eden, lush with pleasant trees bearing good fruit, the tree of life and the tree of knowledge standing in its middle. A single river issues from Eden, parting into four streams that water the ground. Soft green grass and fertile dark soil, with reeds along the banks. At the eastern edge, a boundary of cherubim and a flaming sword.

fields.timeOfDay: Late evening dusk, warm gold light fading toward cool grey, still clear air with a faint dry wind

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

canon.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
canon.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

quotes.quote: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron
Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
canon.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
canon.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

quotes.quote: made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet. They made them with cherubim
He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle.

canon.name: Laban
canon.note: Brother of Rebekah in Haran; hosts Jacob, gives him Leah and Rachel, and makes a covenant with him at Gilead.

stages.label: Laban of Haran

quotes.quote: Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.
When Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house.

stages.text: Laban: a man in his middle years, past youth but vigorous, with a sturdy build from herding and travel. Skin weathered olive-brown. Dark hair cropped close at the neck, a short full beard greying at the chin. Calm, watchful eyes and a broad, lined face. Signature outfit: a long undergarment of undyed wool beneath a rust-red wool mantle, leather sandals, a leather belt at the waist. Carries a herdsman's staff of dark wood.

canon.name: Jacob
canon.note: Younger twin son of Isaac and Rebekah, renamed Israel after wrestling with God and father of the twelve sons; the central patriarch of Genesis, also referenced by name in Hosea, Obadiah, Malachi and the New Testament letters.

stages.label: Jacob

quotes.quote: The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
Isn’t he rightly named Jacob?
his hand had hold on Esau’s heel
leaning on the top of his staff.

stages.text: Jacob: a slender, wiry man of middle to later years in his prime and sixties-to-seventies in old age; lean, sinewy build from long herding; smooth, unhairy skin browned by sun; dark, close-cropped hair and short beard kept trim; alert, thoughtful eyes and a clean, quiet face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and wool wrap cloak in earth brown, with leather sandals. Carries a shepherd's staff.

canon.name: Rachel
canon.note: Younger daughter of Laban, beloved wife of Jacob, mother of Joseph and Benjamin; dies in childbirth.

stages.label: Rachel

quotes.quote: Rachel was beautiful in form and attractive.
Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she kept them.

stages.text: Rachel: a young woman of about eighteen to twenty-five, slender and graceful, of good height; warm olive-brown skin, dark almond eyes, full dark brown hair worn long and bound with a linen band; fine, attractive features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a deep indigo wool wrap over the shoulders, simple leather sandals. Signature prop: a wooden shepherd's staff.

canon.name: Gilead
canon.note: Mountain in Gilead where Laban and Jacob make their covenant; the Genesis Gilead, not any other mountain here.

stages.label: Gilead, mountain country

quotes.quote: he rose up, passed over the River, and set his face toward the mountain of Gilead.
Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Laban with his relatives encamped in the mountain of Gilead.
a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing spices and balm and myrrh

stages.text: Gilead: high rocky mountain country east of the River, terraced hillsides of grey limestone and red earth, scattered oak and terebinth, wild grass and thorn scrub, dry watercourses between ridges, distant hills fading to blue, a few mud-brick and stone shelters at the edges, goat tracks, balm and spice shrubs on the slopes.

fields.primarySubject: Laban standing upright, gesturing with open hands in indignant complaint
fields.action: Laban confronts Jacob, rebuking him for fleeing in secret and deceiving him
fields.setting: Rocky hill country of Gilead with tents pitched among scrub and terebinth trees
fields.secondaryElements: Jacob standing firm with a staff; Rachel near the tent entrance; a herd of flocks grazing on the slope; travel cloaks and packed goods piled nearby
fields.mood: Tense, wounded anger giving way to grief and wounded pride
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon, sun low and warm with dust drifting in the dry air
fields.composition: Medium shot from the side, Laban and Jacob facing each other across the open ground with the tents behind them

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

canon.name: Simon Peter
canon.note: The fisherman apostle, first-called disciple and leader of the twelve, who appears in the Gospels, Acts, Galatians and both letters of Peter; all entries here are the same individual, distinguished only by role and portrayal.

stages.label: Simon Peter

quotes.quote: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas

stages.text: Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.

canon.name: James son of Zebedee
canon.note: Fisherman disciple called with his brother John in Matthew; distinct from James son of Alphaeus.

stages.label: James son of Zebedee

quotes.quote: James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets.
James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);

stages.text: James son of Zebedee: a man in his late twenties to thirties; lean, strong build from hauling nets; weathered olive-brown skin; short dark curly hair and a close-trimmed beard; steady, earnest eyes and a sun-lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown with a dark wool cloak in faded blue-grey. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

canon.name: John the apostle, son of Zebedee
canon.note: Fisherman apostle, brother of James son of Zebedee, appearing in Matthew, Luke and Acts; distinct from John the Baptist and John Mark.

stages.label: John the apostle

quotes.quote: in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets
who were partners with Simon

stages.text: John the apostle: young man of about twenty-five to thirty; lean, strong fisherman's build; sun-browned skin; dark brown hair falling to the shoulders, short beard; clear, earnest eyes and a steady, youthful face. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in earth tones with a dark brown wool cloak, sleeves rolled. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

canon.name: The Twelve Disciples (collective)
canon.note: The twelve apostles/disciples as one collective body acting together across the Gospels and Acts; distinct from the individual disciples named within them.

stages.label: The Twelve Disciples (collective)

stages.text: The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

aliases: the place where they went to pray
canon.name: Gethsemane
canon.note: Garden where Jesus prays and is arrested, named in Matthew and Mark; in Luke the same place is called the garden on the mount, on the Mount of Olives, so it is one place with three names.

stages.label: Gethsemane

quotes.quote: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane
They came to a place which was named Gethsemane.

stages.text: Gethsemane: a walled garden on the slope of the Mount of Olives, above the city of Jerusalem. Ancient gnarled olive trees with silver-grey leaves and thick trunks; dry limestone and red earth underfoot; low stone wall with a wooden gate; a press-stone and rough stone terrace; pale rock outcrops at the edge.

fields.primarySubject: Jesus standing, half-turned, one hand lifted in a gesture of quiet instruction toward the seated disciples.
fields.action: Jesus gives the instruction to sit and wait while he goes apart to pray.
fields.setting: A rough olive grove on the slope of the Mount of Olives, gnarled trees and uneven stone ground.
fields.secondaryElements: Eleven disciples settled on the ground in a loose group under the trees, some leaning on their cloaks; a few olive branches overhead.
fields.mood: Solemn, quiet, expectant, with a sense of coming separation.
fields.timeOfDay: Late night under clear, still air with a few drifting clouds; dim moonlight through the branches and a faint glow of torches from the city below.
fields.composition: Viewed from slightly behind and to the side of the disciples, Jesus placed in the middle distance facing away toward the deeper grove, with the seated group in the foreground.

stages.label: Ezekiel son of Buzi

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ

canon.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
canon.name: Jerusalem
canon.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

fields.primarySubject: Ezekiel standing in the gap of the broken wall, head lifted and arms slightly open in a searching gesture

fields.secondaryElements: Scattered figures of townsfolk in worn tunics and cloaks keeping their distance on the streets below; dust and rubble on the paving; a distant radiance veiled in slowly moving cloud, its fire-like glow at the heart, lighting the gap.

fields.timeOfDay: Dusk deepening into night under still, heavy air, with low drifting cloud and faint smoke over the city.
fields.composition: Wide view from below the broken wall, Ezekiel centered in the gap, the city receding behind him and the veiled radiance rising in the upper distance.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. canon.name: Joab
canon.note: Son of Zeruiah and David's army commander, who kills Abner, Absalom and Amasa and leads the Ammonite campaign; distinguish from other Joabs by his role as David's commander in the army.

stages.label: Joab, captain of David's army

canon.name: Benaiah son of Jehoiada (Kings)
canon.note: Captain of David's army and guard who carries out Solomon's executions in 1 Kings; the same Benaiah son of Jehoiada named here as one of the mighty men and later bodyguard commander.

stages.label: Benaiah son of Jehoiada

quotes.quote: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds

stages.text: Benaiah son of Jehoiada: a seasoned man of about forty to fifty, broad-shouldered and sturdy from years of combat, with dark skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard shot with grey, a weathered, steady face with a firm mouth and deep-set eyes. His signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic under a dark brown wool cloak with a deep red border, with bronze scale armour and a leather belt; he wears a bronze helmet. He carries a bronze-headed spear and a curved sword.

canon.note: The land of Egypt where patriarchs sojourn, Israel is enslaved and plagues fall; recurs in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Psalms, Ezekiel, Hosea, Micah and Hebrews as the same land.

quotes.quote: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land.

stages.text: Egypt: a long green valley of the Nile flanked by pale desert; broad river channels, canals and reed marsh; fertile black earth fields of barley and flax; date palms and sycamores; mud-brick and limestone cities with tall temple pylons, obelisks and fortified walls; the Delta with its towns of Goshen and Zoan.

fields.secondaryElements: Scattered hailstones on fields and fallen palm fronds; a small Israelite settlement with families in dust-stained tunics and cloaks at the edge of the land.

fields.timeOfDay: Daytime storm; the sky is darkened by cloud and light is harsh, broken by lightning flashes.

canon.name: Moses
canon.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

canon.name: The priests and Levites (Deuteronomy)
canon.note: The Levitical priests who bear the ark and minister and judge in Deuteronomy's ritual and legal scenes.

stages.label: The priests and Levites

quotes.quote: the priests the sons of Levi, who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant
You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant

stages.text: The priests and Levites: adult men of middle age, sturdy and dignified; olive-brown skin of the Levant; close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard; calm, grave features. canon.name: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy
canon.note: Tribal judges and officers who hear cases and receive the law in Deuteronomy.

stages.label: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy

quotes.quote: then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges

canon.name: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim
canon.note: The twin mountains in Deuteronomy where blessings and curses are proclaimed; distinct from the Judges Mount Gerizim, which is the same mountain only by name and is kept apart as a separate setting of Jotham's parable.

stages.label: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim

quotes.quote: you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim, and the curse on Mount Ebal.
These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people
These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse

stages.text: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim: two bare limestone ridges of the central hill country rising opposite each other across a narrow valley. canon.name: The plains of Moab
canon.note: Eastern camp across the Jordan where Moses speaks the law and dies, Deuteronomy only.

stages.label: The plains of Moab

quotes.quote: Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to declare this law

in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites

all that is done under the sky

stages.text: Under the sun: a wide, sun-bleached Levantine earth of dry hill country and terraced fields, with stone walls, olive and terebinth trees, winding river beds, and distant walled cities of pale limestone beneath an open sky.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

canon.name: The Twelve Disciples (collective)
canon.note: The twelve apostles/disciples as one collective body acting together across the Gospels and Acts; distinct from the individual disciples named within them.

stages.label: The Twelve Disciples (collective)

quotes.quote: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

stages.text: The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

canon.name: Capernaum
canon.note: The lakeside town in Galilee where Jesus lives, teaches and heals, with a synagogue and Simon Peter's house; all four Gospels' entries describe this one place.

stages.label: Capernaum

quotes.quote: Leaving Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali
They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.
They entered into the boat, and were going over the sea to Capernaum.

stages.text: Capernaum: a fishing town of plain basalt and limestone houses with flat roofs, packed close along a curving shore of the Sea of Galilee. A white limestone synagogue with a tall carved doorway stands near the water, its pillars facing the lake. Nearby, a modest family house of stone with a courtyard and reed-thatched roof marks Simon's home. Fishing boats are drawn up on the stones, nets hung on poles. Olive trees, palms and fig trees grow on the slopes behind the town, with dry hills rising beyond.

fields.primarySubject: Jesus seated, one hand resting on a small child standing beside him
fields.action: Jesus gently welcomes the child into his embrace as he speaks to the gathered disciples
fields.setting: Plain plastered stone house interior in Capernaum with a low table
fields.secondaryElements: Twelve disciples in undyed tunics and earth-toned cloaks around Jesus, attentive and still; oil lamp unlit on a wall niche
fields.mood: Tender, reverent and quietly instructive
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon indoors, clear warm Galilean air, light fading toward evening
fields.composition: Eye-level view from the room's side, Jesus and child centered, disciples arranged in a half-circle around them

moment.text: Every man has become brutish and without knowledge. Every goldsmith is disappointed by his engraved image; for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.

previous.text: When he utters his voice, the waters in the heavens roar, and he causes the vapors to ascend from the ends of the earth. He makes lightnings for the rain, and brings the wind out of his treasuries.

next.text: They are vanity, a work of delusion. In the time of their visitation they will perish.

section.title: Against idols and prayer for mercy

canon.name: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah
canon.note: Prophet from Anathoth who speaks most of the book.

stages.label: Jeremiah

quotes.quote: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
They let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

stages.text: Jeremiah: a man in his middle years, lean and weathered from long journeys and imprisonment, with a grave, careworn face and deep-set dark eyes. Close-cropped dark hair and a short greying beard. Dark-skinned Levantine complexion. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a long brown wool cloak, the cloak worn thin at the hem. Carries a plain wooden staff.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
canon.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
canon.name: Jerusalem
canon.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

fields.primarySubject: A goldsmith seated at a workbench, shoulders slumped, staring at a lifeless molten idol.
fields.action: The goldsmith turns away from his failed image, hands open in despair, as Jeremiah stands in the doorway.
fields.setting: A small city workshop inside Jerusalem's walls with clay crucibles, bronze tools and a cooling furnace.
fields.secondaryElements: Jeremiah in a plain tunic and cloak at the doorway; an unfinished metal idol with no life; scattered tools and scrolls on a shelf.
fields.mood: Grief, disappointment and quiet sobriety.
fields.timeOfDay: Dim overcast afternoon, grey light slowly fading, dust hanging in the air.
fields.composition: Interior view from the doorway, with the goldsmith and idol in the foreground and Jeremiah framed at the edge.

moment.text: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”

previous.text: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”

next.text: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”

section.title: Agrippa's response; Paul's words to the court

canon.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
canon.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

canon.name: King Agrippa
canon.note: Herodian king who hears Paul's defense.

stages.label: King Agrippa

quotes.quote: King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp

stages.text: King Agrippa: a man in his early forties; lean, upright build; olive skin; dark hair cut short and a neatly trimmed dark beard with grey at the chin; composed, watchful face with heavy brows. Signature outfit: a fine white linen tunic under a purple-bordered royal cloak of deep violet, with a gold fibula at the shoulder. Carries a plain ceremonial staff of dark wood with a gold cap.

canon.name: Bernice
canon.note: Sister of King Agrippa who attends the hearing with him.

stages.label: Bernice

quotes.quote: King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp

stages.text: Bernice: a woman of about forty, dignified and composed; olive-brown skin; dark hair drawn up and bound with gold pins beneath a fine linen veil edged in purple; a tall, straight-backed build; a poised, aristocratic face with dark, steady eyes. Signature outfit: a long layered tunic of deep purple wool under a pale ivory mantle with a gold-thread border. Signature prop: a slim gold diadem at her brow.

canon.name: Porcius Festus
canon.note: Roman governor who succeeds Felix and refers Paul's case to King Agrippa; a different governor from Pilate and from Gedaliah.

stages.label: Porcius Festus

quotes.quote: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

stages.text: Porcius Festus: a man of about fifty, middle-aged and of sturdy, practical build; olive-brown skin; short dark hair with grey at the temples, closely cropped; a clean-shaven face with a firm jaw and a thoughtful, weathered brow. Signature outfit: a deep purple-edged white toga over a plain ochre tunic, with a bronze fibula at the shoulder. Signature prop: a small wax writing tablet bound in leather.

canon.name: Caesarea Maritima
canon.note: Coastal Roman port city on the Mediterranean, where Cornelius lives, Herod dies, and Paul is held; distinct from Caesarea Philippi in the north.

stages.label: Caesarea Maritima

quotes.quote: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,
he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat

stages.text: Caesarea Maritima: a Roman port city on the Mediterranean coast of Judea, built of pale limestone and mortar. A broad curved harbour with stone moles and wooden-hulled fishing boats, a white-stone city of colonnaded streets, a Roman theatre facing the sea, administrative halls, and bathhouses with arched roofs. Low sea grasses and palms along the shore, dry Mediterranean scrub on the inland rise.

fields.primarySubject: King Agrippa seated on a raised throne, body turned toward Paul with a startled, probing expression.
fields.action: Agrippa reacts with a sharp, half-mocking challenge while Paul stands chained, listening.
fields.setting: Audience hall of the governor's palace in Caesarea Maritima, marble floors and stone columns with arched openings.
fields.secondaryElements: Festus seated nearby in Roman dress, Bernice in royal robes beside Agrippa, tribunes in armor, soldiers at the edges, chains on Paul's wrists.
fields.mood: Tense, intimate and charged, with a flicker of wry resistance in the king.
fields.timeOfDay: Afternoon, clear warm Mediterranean day, bright sunlight streaming through high windows and arches.
fields.composition: Wide view from the side of the hall, Agrippa on the raised throne at right, Paul standing center-left facing him, court arrayed around them.

next.text: For entangled like thorns, and drunken as with their drink, they are consumed utterly like dry stubble.

canon.name: Nineveh (Assyrian capital)
canon.note: The Assyrian capital city of Nineveh; all four entries refer to the same city, appearing in Isaiah, Jonah, Nahum and Zephaniah, and are joined as one place.

stages.label: Nineveh, the great Assyrian capital

quotes.quote: The populous city will be deserted. The hill and the watchtower will be for dens forever
The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.
Nineveh has been from of old like a pool of water
make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as the wilderness.

stages.text: Nineveh: a vast walled Assyrian capital on a broad plain beside great rivers, with high mud-brick walls, towering gates of cut stone with winged bull guardians, a royal palace on a raised mound, and a watchtower on a hill. Its moats and river gates hold water like a pool. Date palms, reeds and irrigated fields line the riverbanks; the later ruins are dry, windswept wilderness with dens and wild grass.

fields.primarySubject: Assyrian counselors in fringed royal robes gathered in a palace courtyard, faces lifted toward the sky.
fields.action: They confer in urgent gestures while the radiance above the walls brightens and the cloud begins to part.
fields.setting: The walled palace district of Nineveh with massive stone gates, towers and wide courtyards.
fields.secondaryElements: Soldiers in period armor and helmets along the walls; torchlight on the palace walls; a fire-like glow at the heart of the radiance, with the cloud-veiled presence of God above the city.
fields.mood: Tense, foreboding and solemn, with rising dread.
fields.timeOfDay: Late dusk shifting toward deep night under heavy storm clouds with dry wind stirring dust.
fields.composition: Low viewpoint from the courtyard, looking up across the walls toward the radiance filling the upper sky.

moment.text: But when the cloud began to arise up out of the city in a pillar of smoke, the Benjamites looked behind them; and behold, the whole city went up in smoke to the sky.

previous.text: The men of Israel turned in the battle, and Benjamin began to strike and kill of the men of Israel about thirty persons; for they said, “Surely they are struck down before us, as in the first battle.”

next.text: The men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were dismayed; for they saw that disaster had come on them.

section.title: War against Benjamin

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
canon.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
canon.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

canon.name: Tribe of Benjamin
canon.note: The Benjamite tribe as a collective in Judges, nearly destroyed in the Gibeah war and rebuilt by seizing wives at Shiloh; not an individual, so kept apart from Benjamin the son of Jacob.

stages.label: Tribe of Benjamin

quotes.quote: The children of Benjamin were counted on that day out of the cities twenty-six thousand men who drew the sword

stages.text: Tribe of Benjamin: men of fighting age and mature adults, lean and sinewy from farming and war; sun-browned olive skin; short dark beards and cropped hair, some with a headband; serious, weathered faces; a plain woven wool tunic in undyed brown and cream under a rust-red cloak; carries a sling or short sword.

aliases: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
canon.name: Phinehas son of Eleazar
canon.note: Priest, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron; appears in Numbers (Baal Peor, Midian), Joshua (Jordan altar dispute) and Judges (Benjamin war at Bethel). Same priestly lineage and role across all three, so one individual.

stages.label: Phinehas, priest of the Aaronic line

quotes.quote: he rose up from the middle of the congregation, and took a spear in his hand.
to the war, with the vessels of the sanctuary and the trumpets for the alarm in his hand.

stages.text: Phinehas: a man in middle age, strong and steady, of Israelite desert-born build; olive-brown skin; dark hair and a short trimmed beard streaked with grey; calm, weathered face. Signature outfit: a white linen priestly tunic with a blue-violet robe and a linen mitre. Carries a spear and the sanctuary trumpets.

aliases: the husband of the murdered woman
the man from the hill country of Ephraim
canon.name: The Levite husband of the concubine
canon.note: Levite from the hill country of Ephraim whose concubine is abused and killed at Gibeah; he cuts her body into twelve pieces. Not the young Levite of Bethlehem who serves Micah.

stages.label: The Levite husband of the concubine

quotes.quote: The Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered

stages.text: The Levite husband of the concubine: a man in his thirties, lean and weathered by travel, with olive skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard shot with grey at the chin. Calm, grave features and steady dark eyes. He wears a plain woven tunic of undyed wool in ochre-brown beneath a long cloak of dusty grey-blue wool. He carries a traveller's staff of dark wood and a leather bag at his hip.

canon.name: Mizpah (Gilead assembly place)
canon.note: The Gileadite gathering place in Judges where Jephthah speaks before Yahweh and the war against Ammon is organized; distinguished by the Judges setting and Gilead context.

stages.label: Mizpah (Gilead assembly place)

quotes.quote: The children of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpah.
Jephthah spoke all his words before Yahweh in Mizpah.

stages.text: Mizpah: a high ridge of pale limestone and red-brown earth in the hill country of Gilead, terraced for gathering. Flat open ground at its crest is ringed by low dry-stone walls and a few squat mud-brick and stone shrines with plain lintels. Scattered terebinth and oak stand at the edges, with olive groves and grey scrub on the slopes below.

canon.name: Bethel (conquered town of Joseph's house)
canon.note: Town in Judges taken by the house of Joseph, also where Israel seeks God's counsel in the war against Benjamin; note the Luz alias here matches the Genesis town, but this entry is the Judges conquest and counsel setting.

stages.label: Bethel (conquered town of Joseph's house)

quotes.quote: The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and Yahweh was with them.
The man went into the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called its name Luz
between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim
went up to Bethel, and asked counsel of God.

stages.text: Bethel: a walled hill town in the highlands of Ephraim on a stony ridge above a highway running north to Shechem and south toward Gibeah. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs stand close together behind a fortified gate and rough stone wall. Terraced slopes bear olive and fig trees, with scrub oak on the rocky ridges. A high place with standing stones marks the sacred ground where the people seek counsel.

canon.name: Gibeah of Benjamin (Judges)
canon.note: The Benjamite city where the Levite's concubine is abused and killed and that is the scene of the war against Benjamin in Judges; distinguish from Saul's Gibeah in 1 Samuel by the Judges events of the concubine and the war.

stages.label: Gibeah of Benjamin

quotes.quote: the sun went down on them near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin
He went in, and sat down in the street of the city
The children of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.

stages.text: Gibeah of Benjamin: a fortified hill town of the Benjamite highlands, set on a rocky ridge with terraced slopes. Low houses of mud brick and stone stand close together along a narrow street, flat roofs, and a city wall with a gate. Olive trees, vines and scrub grow on the slopes, with open fields and highways running out of the town.

fields.primarySubject: Benjamite warriors halted on the field, turning and looking back over their shoulders
fields.action: Smoke billows upward from the burning town, and the Benjamites realize their city is ablaze
fields.setting: Open fields below the fortified hill town of Gibeah, with ridges and tents of Israel in the distance
fields.secondaryElements: Israelite fighters turning to strike in the foreground, the city walls glowing orange with fire, a dark column of smoke rising into the sky
fields.mood: Stunned dismay, grave and sorrowful, with the weight of disaster falling on the Benjamites
fields.timeOfDay: Late day at dusk, with a clear dry sky and warm orange light from the flames
fields.composition: Wide view from the field looking toward the city, with Benjamite figures in the middle ground turned back and the tall smoke column rising at the center

moment.text: Her nobles were purer than snow. They were whiter than milk. They were more ruddy in body than rubies. Their polishing was like sapphire.

previous.text: For the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown as in a moment. No hands were laid on her.

canon.name: Zion
canon.note: Personified city of Jerusalem as a mourning widow and captive princess, speaking in the first person in Lamentations 1 and 2; distinct from the collective people of Judah and Jerusalem.

stages.label: Zion, the mourning city-woman

quotes.quote: She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations!
All her gates are desolate. Her priests sigh.
They have clothed themselves with sackcloth. The virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

stages.text: Zion: a woman of middle years, dignified and grieving, with dark hair bound low and partly veiled, olive skin darkened by ash and dust. Her features are worn and sorrowful. She wears a plain undyed linen robe under a dark sackcloth mantle of brown and grey, with a torn hem. She carries no regalia.

canon.name: Children of Zion (Lamentations)
canon.note: Infants and children who faint in the streets or beg for bread in Lamentations.

stages.label: Children of Zion

quotes.quote: the young children and the infants swoon in the streets of the city
The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold
The tongue of the nursing child clings to the roof of his mouth for thirst.

stages.text: Children of Zion: young boys and girls aged about four to twelve, with slight thin builds worn down by hunger; olive to brown skin dulled with dust; dark hair cropped short or tied back; large dark eyes and sunken cheeks. Plain undyed linen or wool tunics belted with cord, faded to grey-brown, bare feet dusty. Signature prop: a small clay jar or pitcher held close.

canon.name: The priests of Jerusalem
canon.note: Collective body of priests in Lamentations who are killed in the sanctuary; a group, not an individual.

stages.label: Priests of Jerusalem

quotes.quote: Her priests sigh.
Should the priest and the prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?

stages.text: The priests of Jerusalem: men of middle to later years, lean and dignified, with dark-brown skin, short dark hair and a neatly kept beard flecked with grey. Calm, grave faces marked by sorrow. Signature outfit: a white linen priestly tunic and a linen headband, with a blue-violet cloak over the shoulders. Carry only a bronze censer.

canon.name: Prophets of Jerusalem
canon.note: The prophets of Jerusalem who gave false visions and are blamed for the city's fall, as portrayed in Lamentations.

stages.label: Prophets of Jerusalem

quotes.quote: her prophets find no vision from Yahweh
the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests

stages.text: Prophets of Jerusalem: men in middle age, lean and weathered, with dark skin tanned by sun and a sturdy build. Short dark beards, hair cropped at the neck, deep-set attentive eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a dull ochre wool cloak. Each carries a plain wooden staff.

canon.name: The enemies (Jerusalem's foreign adversaries)
canon.note: Collective invaders and persecutors who destroy Jerusalem in Lamentations; a human/national group, not the divine accuser, so keep separate from Satan.

stages.label: The enemies (Jerusalem's foreign adversaries)

quotes.quote: Her adversaries have become the head. Her enemies prosper

stages.text: The enemies: adult men of the Mesopotamian and neighbouring Levantine peoples, aged twenty to fifty, lean and hardened by campaign. Skin weathered tan to olive-brown. Hair short or bound back, beards trimmed close. Stern, watchful faces. Typical dress: a sleeveless or short-sleeved tunic of undyed wool with a leather belt, a bronze-scaled or leather armour, and a dusty brown cloak. Colours: ochre, rust and iron-grey. Carries a spear or curved sword; no other props.

canon.name: The streets of the city
canon.note: Streets and roads where the children faint, the dead lie and the blind wander.

stages.label: The streets of the city

quotes.quote: The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to the solemn assembly.
All her gates are desolate.
The stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the head of every street.

stages.text: The streets of the city: narrow, unpaved or rough-stoned lanes winding between low flat-roofed houses of mud brick and dressed limestone, with broken walls and ruined doorways. Dust and ash lie thick; some stones of the sanctuary and fallen gold-toned debris lie at the corners. Sparse dry scrub grows in cracks, and gates stand desolate at the end of roads leading up toward Zion.

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion
the house of Yahweh of Armies
canon.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
canon.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

aliases: Edom in the land of Uz
canon.name: The wilderness and exile
canon.note: The Lamentations setting of captivity, pursuit and hiding where the exiles dwell or are hunted; a different place from the Egyptian prison despite the shared alias 'the dungeon'.

stages.label: The wilderness and exile

quotes.quote: She dwells among the nations. She finds no rest.
They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and have cast a stone on me.
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Yahweh, was taken in their pits

stages.text: The wilderness and exile: arid highland and dry steppe under a pale sky, scattered with stony ravines, cisterns cut into rock, and low flat-roofed mud-brick dwellings and walled settlements of foreign towns. Sparse thorn scrub and dry grass, a few gnarled terebinths, and distant ruined walls of a broken city on the horizon.

fields.primarySubject: Nobles of Jerusalem standing upright in worn but once-fine court robes, and Zion, a grieving woman in sackcloth, seated among ash.
fields.action: The nobles stand still and dignified while Zion bows her head in lament, the moment held without movement.
fields.setting: Scorched street of Jerusalem with ruined walls and dust-strewn stone.
fields.secondaryElements: Children of Zion in faded tunics standing near the nobles, thin and hunger-worn, with radiance without source veiled by cloud above the scene.
fields.mood: Grief tempered by remembered dignity, reverent and solemn.
fields.timeOfDay: Smoke-dimmed late afternoon with hot, still air and drifting ash.
fields.composition: Mid-distance view across the street, nobles on the left, Zion in the foreground right, the veiled light high above.
